Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 57, verse 1:

(p-5670) In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

Surah al-Hadid (The Iron)

It was named thus because it supports (nasir) Allah and His Messenger in jihad. It was therefore treated as the verses that support Allah and His Messenger, in that it is a cause for establishing justice, like the Qur'an. Also, it gathers together many benefits, and so it resembles that too. Thus a surah in which this is mentioned was named after it. This is from al-Mahayimi.

It is Medinan according to the more correct view. Indeed, al-Naqqash said: it is Medinan by the consensus of the exegetes. The arrangement of its verses and what they point to confirms this conclusively.

Its number of verses is twenty-nine.

Imam Ahmad narrated from 'Irbad ibn Sariyah that "the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to recite the Musabbihat before he slept, and he said: 'Among them is a verse better than a thousand verses.'" Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i narrated it in the same way.

Ibn Kathir said: the verse referred to in the hadith is, Allah knows best, His saying, ﴿He is the First and the Last﴾ [al-Hadid: 3], and so on, for reasons that will come later. Allah knows best.

(p-5671) In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

[1] ﴿Whatever is in the heavens and the earth glorifies Allah, and He is the Mighty, the Wise.﴾

﴿Whatever is in the heavens and the earth glorifies Allah﴾ meaning: every existing thing manifests His transcendence above partners and offspring, and everything that is unfitting for Him, and it indicates His singularity in divinity, His governance, His knowledge and His power. For whoever witnesses this world with all its created beings in a state of order and precision, the linking of causes to effects, and the transformation of some existing things into others, whose wonders never cease and whose ends are never exhausted, will inevitably conclude that this firmly ordered arrangement is the work of one Creator, governing its system, willing its course according to its laws, as we have expounded in "Proofs of Monotheism" (Dala'il al-Tawhid).

﴿And He is the Mighty﴾ meaning: the Powerful who subdues everything in the heavens and the earth. ﴿the Wise﴾ meaning: the One who arranged the system of every existing thing in a judicious order.

The discussion of His saying, may He be exalted:

[2] ﴿To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He gives life and causes death, and He is over all things competent.﴾

﴿To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾: that is, their sovereignty, and the authority of command over them is executed. ﴿He gives life and causes death﴾: that is, He brings into existence whatever He wills of animals and plants however He wills, and He causes it to die after it reaches its appointed term, so He brings it to an end. ﴿And He is over all things competent﴾: that is, perfect in power, so nothing He wills is beyond Him, whether giving life, causing death, or anything else.

**Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil, "The Beauties of Interpretation") on Surah 57, Verse 3**

The discussion of the interpretation (ta'wil) of His saying, Exalted is He:

[3] ﴿He is the First and the Last, and the Manifest and the Hidden, and He is Knowing of all things.﴾

﴿He is the First﴾ means: the One who precedes every existing thing, in that He is its originator and its creator. ﴿and the Last﴾ (p-٥٦٧٢) means: the One who remains after the perishing of everything. ﴿and the Manifest﴾ means: His existence is evident through the proofs that indicate it. Ibn Jarir said: it means the One who is above everything other than Him, and He is exalted above everything, so nothing is higher than Him. ﴿and the Hidden﴾ means: He is concealed by His essence and His reality, or He is the One who knows the inner reality of everything. Ibn Jarir said: it means the One who is inwardly aware of all things, so nothing is closer to anything than He is, as He said: ﴿And We are closer to him than his jugular vein﴾ [Qaf: 16]. ﴿And He is Knowing of all things﴾ means: He has perfect knowledge, so nothing is hidden from Him.

Imam Ahmad narrated from Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to supplicate at bedtime: "O Allah, Lord of the seven heavens and Lord of the Mighty Throne, our Lord and the Lord of all things, Revealer of the Torah, the Gospel and the Qur'an, Splitter of the grain and the date-stone, there is no god but You. I seek refuge in You from the evil of every evil-doer whose forelock You hold. You are the First, so there is nothing before You; You are the Last, so there is nothing after You; You are the Manifest, so there is nothing above You; You are the Hidden, so there is nothing beneath You. Settle our debt for us and enrich us from poverty." Narrated by Muslim and others.

The Discussion on the Interpretation of His Words, the Exalted:

[4] ﴿He it is who created the heavens and the earth in six days; then He established Himself upon the Throne. He knows what enters into the earth and what comes out of it, and what descends from the sky and what ascends into it. And He is with you wherever you are. And Allah is Seeing of what you do.﴾

﴿He it is who created the heavens and the earth in six days﴾ Al-Qashani said: That is, of the divine days. It was said: [they are] the known days. And Allah knows best.

﴿Then He established Himself upon the Throne﴾ Ibn Jarir said: (p-5673) That is: He it is who brought into being the seven heavens and the earths, and arranged them and what is in them; then He established Himself upon His Throne, rising over it and exalting Himself.

﴿He knows what enters into the earth﴾ That is, of His creation, such as the dead, the seeds and the animals. ﴿And what comes out of it﴾ That is, such as the crops. ﴿And what descends from the sky﴾ That is, of the rains, snows, hail, decrees and rulings. ﴿And what ascends into it﴾ That is, of the angels, deeds and other things. ﴿And He is with you wherever you are﴾ Ibn Jarir said: That is, He is witnessing you wherever you are; He knows you, knows your deeds, your movements and your dwelling places, while He is upon His Throne above His seven heavens.

Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah have mercy on him, said in his "Sharh Hadith al-Nuzul": The word "ma'iyyah" (being with) in Surah al-Hadid and in al-Mujadilah, in their two verses, its interpretation is established from the early generation (al-salaf) as knowledge. They said: He is with them by His knowledge. Imam Ibn Abd al-Barr and others have mentioned that this is a consensus of the Companions and the Successors who followed them in excellence, and no one whose opinion is considered has opposed them. It is reported from Ibn Abbas, al-Dahhak, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, Sufyan al-Thawri, Ahmad ibn Hanbal and others. Ibn Abi Hatim said, from Ibn Abbas regarding this verse: "He is upon the Throne and His knowledge is with them," and likewise for those mentioned with him. Imam Ahmad expounded the discussion of ma'iyyah in "al-Radd ala al-Jahmiyyah." The word ma'iyyah in the Book of Allah has come in a general sense, as in these two verses, and has come in a specific sense, as in His words:

﴿Indeed, Allah is with those who fear Him and those who are doers of good﴾ [al-Nahl: 128], and His words:

﴿Indeed, I am with you both; I hear and I see﴾ [Ta-Ha: 46], and His words: ﴿Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us﴾ [al-Tawbah: 40]. Had it been intended that He is with everything by His essence, the generality would contradict the specification, for it is known that His words ﴿Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us﴾ [al-Tawbah: 40] intended by it His specifying Himself and Abu Bakr, to the exclusion of their enemies among the disbelievers. Likewise His words ﴿Indeed, Allah is with those who fear Him and those who are doers of good﴾ [al-Nahl: 128] singled them out, to the exclusion of the wrongdoers and the wicked. Furthermore, the word ma'iyyah is not used in the Arabic language, nor anywhere in the Qur'an, to mean the mixing of one essence with another, as in His words: ﴿Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and those with him﴾ [al-Fath: 29], and His words: ﴿Then those are with the believers﴾ [al-Nisa': 146], and His words: ﴿Fear Allah and be with the truthful﴾ [al-Tawbah: 119], and His words: ﴿and strive with your wealth and your lives﴾ [al-Anfal: 72], and the like of this is numerous. Furthermore, it is impossible that His words ﴿and He is with you﴾ indicate that His essence is mixed with the essences of creation. Furthermore, He began the verse with knowledge and ended it with knowledge, so the context indicates that He intended that He is aware of it. He expounded on this matter in another place, and clarified that the word ma'iyyah in the language, although it implies companionship and proximity, when it is with the servants it does not contradict His being elevated over His Throne, and the ruling of His being with them differs according to each situation: He is with all of creation by knowledge, power and dominion, and He specifies some of them with help, victory and support. End of quote.

Imam Muwaffaq al-Din Ibn Qudamah al-Maqdisi, may Allah be pleased with him, said in "Dhamm al-Ta'wil":

If it is said: You have interpreted verses and reports, saying regarding His words ﴿and He is with you wherever you are﴾ that it means by knowledge, and similar verses and reports, so what applies to us applies to you?

We say: We have not interpreted anything, and carrying these expressions upon these meanings is not interpretation, because ta'wil is turning the expression away from its apparent sense, and these meanings are the apparent sense of these expressions, as evidenced by their being what comes first to the understanding from them. The apparent sense of an expression is what comes first to the understanding from it, whether it is literal or figurative. This is why the apparent sense of conventional terms is the figurative rather than the literal, such as the terms "riwayah" and "zaʿinah" and other conventional terms, for the apparent sense of these is the figurative and not the literal, and turning them to the literal would be interpretation requiring evidence. Likewise, terms that have a legal convention and a linguistic literal meaning, such as wudu', tahara, salah, sawm, zakah and hajj, their apparent sense is only the legal convention and not the linguistic literal meaning. Given that this is established, what comes first to the understanding from the saying "Allah is with you" (p-5675) is: by protection and safeguarding. This is why He, the Exalted, said regarding what He related about His Prophet: ﴿when he said to his companion, "Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us"﴾ [al-Tawbah: 40], and said to Musa: ﴿Indeed, I am with you both; I hear and I see﴾ [Ta-Ha: 46]. Had He intended that He is by His essence with everyone, there would be no special distinction for them in that, since His being is with others just as it is with them, and this would not necessitate the removal of grief from Abu Bakr, nor would it be a cause for it. So it is known that the apparent sense of these expressions is what they have been carried upon, and it is therefore not interpretation. Moreover, even if it were interpretation, it is not what we have interpreted; rather the early generation, may Allah have mercy on them, whose correctness is established and whose following is obligatory, are the ones who interpreted it. Ibn Abbas, al-Dahhak, Malik, Sufyan and many scholars said regarding His words ﴿and He is with you﴾: that is His knowledge. Then it has been established by the Book of Allah, the mutawatir reports from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the consensus of the early generation, that Allah, the Exalted, is in the heaven upon His Throne, and this expression came with surrounding indicators that point to the intended meaning being knowledge: that is His words ﴿Do you not see that Allah knows what is in the heavens and what is on the earth?﴾ [al-Mujadilah: 7], then He said at its end: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Knowing of all things﴾ [al-Mujadilah: 7]. So He began it with knowledge and ended it with it. Then its context is to warn them with Allah's knowledge of their condition, and that He will inform them of what they did on the Day of Resurrection and will recompense them for it. These are all indicators pointing to the intended meaning of knowledge; these indicators coincide in it, and the indication of the reports upon its meaning, and the statements of the early generation and their interpretation. So how could there be attached to it what contradicts the Book, the reports, and the statements of the early generation? This is not hidden from any intelligent person, God willing. And if it is obscure, we have uncovered and clarified it, praise be to Allah, the Exalted. Yet even if a person remains silent about its tafsir and ta'wil, he would not have departed from the truth nor would anything be required of him, for no one is obliged to speak about ta'wil, God willing. End of the words of Ibn Qudamah, may Allah have mercy on him.

﴿And Allah is Seeing of what you do﴾ That is, so He will recompense you for it.

(p-5676)

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 57, verses 5–6:

The explanation of His saying, exalted is He:

[5–6] ﴿To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and to Allah all matters are returned.﴾ ﴿He causes the night to enter into the day and causes the day to enter into the night, and He is Knowing of what is within the breasts.﴾ [al-Hadid: 6]

﴿To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and to Allah all matters are returned.﴾ That is: the affairs of all His creation, so He judges between them by His decree.

﴿He causes the night to enter into the day and causes the day to enter into the night﴾ [al-Hadid: 6]. That is: He makes what is lost from the hours of one of them enter the other, so that it becomes an increase in the other, by His wisdom and His determination. ﴿And He is Knowing of what is within the breasts﴾ [al-Hadid: 6]. That is: of the inner thoughts of the breasts of His servants, and what their souls resolve upon of good or evil.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 57, verses 5–6:

The explanation of His saying, exalted is He:

[5–6] ﴿To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and to Allah all matters are returned.﴾ ﴿He causes the night to enter into the day and causes the day to enter into the night, and He is Knowing of what is within the breasts.﴾ [al-Hadid: 6]

﴿To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and to Allah all matters are returned.﴾ That is: the affairs of all His creation, so He judges between them by His decree.

﴿He causes the night to enter into the day and causes the day to enter into the night﴾ [al-Hadid: 6]. That is: He makes what is lost from the hours of one of them enter the other, so that it becomes an increase in the other, by His wisdom and His determination. ﴿And He is Knowing of what is within the breasts﴾ [al-Hadid: 6]. That is: of the inner thoughts of the breasts of His servants, and what their souls resolve upon of good or evil.

The commentary on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[7] ﴿Believe in Allah and His Messenger, and spend out of that which He has made you successors over. So those among you who believe and spend will have a great reward.﴾

﴿Believe in Allah and His Messenger, and spend out of that which He has made you successors over﴾ That is: believe with certain faith (al-iman al-yaqini), so that its effect may appear upon you, and spending from the wealth of Allah becomes easy for you. He provided it to you and made you successors (mustakhlafin) over it, by empowering you and enabling you to dispose of it according to the ruling of the Sharia (al-shar', sacred law). For all wealth belongs to Allah, and the attribution of disposal specifically to you is only by His ruling in His law. So reported al-Qashani.

Al-Shihab said: "Successorship (al-khilafah) is either from the One who has true disposal, who is Allah, exalted is He, and this is what fits His saying: ﴿To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾ [al-Hadid: 5]; or it is from those who previously disposed of them, from among those who held them and then they passed to you. In either case there is an exhortation to spend and a making light of it. As for the first, it is clear, because He has permitted you to spend from the property of another, and such a thing is easy to give out and to increase. As for the second, also: for whoever knows that it has not remained for those before him, knows that it will not remain for him either, so giving it out becomes easy for him."(p-٥٦٧٧)

؎ Wealth and family are nothing but deposits,
and deposits must one day be returned.

﴿So those among you who believe and spend, for them is a great reward.﴾

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 57, verse 8:

The discussion of His saying, exalted is He:

[8] ﴿And what is [wrong] with you that you do not believe in Allah, while the Messenger calls you to believe in your Lord, and He has already taken your covenant, if you are [truly] believers?﴾

﴿And what is [wrong] with you that you do not believe in Allah﴾: that is, what prevents you from it, when its incentives have become apparent and its paths have been made clear to those who seek them, as He said: ﴿while the Messenger calls you to believe in your Lord﴾: that is, he calls you, by way of reflection and contemplation, to faith in the One who nurtured you with His blessings and turned you about through His favours, so that His thanks became obligatory upon you.

﴿and He has already taken your covenant﴾: that is, to faith, for He endowed you with intellects, set up the proofs for you, and enabled you to reflect. Indeed, He deposited in your natural dispositions (fitrah) that which compels you toward this when you are alerted. This has been accomplished through the reminder of the Messenger, so there remains for you only to set out upon His path.

﴿if you are [truly] believers﴾: al-Qashani said: that is, if the light of the fitrah and of primordial faith still remains within you.

The discussion of His saying, Exalted is He:

[9] ﴿He it is who sends down to His servant clear signs, that He may bring you out from darkness into light. And indeed, Allah is to you Kind and Merciful.﴾

﴿He it is who sends down to His servant clear signs﴾ That is: clear proofs and decisive demonstrations.

﴿That He may bring you out﴾ That is: Allah, or His servant by means of His signs, ﴿from darkness into light﴾ That is: from the darkness of ignorance, disbelief and conflicting desires, into the light of guidance and certainty, which souls perceive and by which hearts find rest. ﴿And indeed, Allah is to you Kind and Merciful﴾ That is, in His sending down of the Books and His sending of the Messengers for your guidance, removing doubts and dispelling confusion.

Since the revelation of this surah was for the command to spend in the way of Allah, and for encouraging and urging it, He mentioned it repeatedly in various forms of exposition and kinds of firm argument. Therefore He, glorified is He, said:

The discussion of the words of His Most High:

[10] ﴿And what is [wrong] with you that you do not spend in the cause of Allah, when to Allah belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth? Not equal among you are those who spent before the conquest and fought. Those are greater in rank than those who spent afterward and fought. But to each Allah has promised the best [reward]. And Allah is Acquainted with what you do.﴾

﴿And what is [wrong] with you that you do not spend in the cause of Allah, when to Allah belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth﴾ That is: He inherits everything in them, and no one will retain wealth. And if that is the case, how fitting it is that a person spend during his life and take it as a store that he will find after his death.

Al-Shihab said: This is among the most eloquent exhortations to spending, for He joined it with faith first, since He commanded them to it, then He rebuked them for abandoning faith despite the clarity of its proofs, and for abandoning spending in the cause of Him who gave it to them, while they were on the brink of death, and it would not remain for them if they did not spend it. The cause of Allah is every good that brings them to Him, more general than jihad and other than it. Some restricted it to jihad, because it is its most perfect instance and its best part, by way of restricting the general to its most important and most comprehensive instances, especially since the occasion of revelation was for that.

﴿Not equal among you are those who spent before the conquest and fought﴾ That is: before the conquest of Makkah, or the treaty of al-Hudaybiyah, and fought so that the word of truth would be exalted. And those who spent afterward and fought, in a time of the strength of Islam and the honour of its people. He omitted the second [party] because the indication of it is clear, for equality is not complete except by mentioning two things. Moreover, it was pointed to by His words, beginning a new statement about them as an added honouring of them: ﴿Those are greater in rank than those who spent afterward and fought﴾ That is: because of the great significance of supporting the Messenger, may Allah's blessings be upon him, with their lives, and spending wealth in that state, when the Muslims were few and the disbelievers had might and great numbers. So the need for support and assistance was more pressing, unlike what came after the conquest, for Islam had by then become strong and disbelief weak. This is indicated by His Most High's words:

﴿And the foremost, the first of the Emigrants and the Helpers, and those who followed them﴾ [al-Tawbah: 100], and by his peace be upon him saying: "Do not revile my Companions, for if one of you spent the like of Uhud in gold, it would not reach a mudd of one of them nor half of it." And this verse indicates the virtue of those who preceded to Islam and spent and strove alongside the Messenger ﷺ, as conveyed by al-Razi.

In al-Iklil: In the verse there is evidence that the Companions have ranks, that the excellence belongs to the one who precedes, that people are placed in their proper stations, and that the excellence of an act is according to the extent to which its benefit returns to Islam and the Muslims, because the reward is according to the measure of the hardship. End.

﴿And to each﴾ That is: and each of the two groups ﴿Allah has promised the best﴾ That is: the best reward, which is Paradise, not only the first group, although among them there is a difference in the degrees of the recompense.

Ibn Kathir said: He mentioned this only so that the other side would not be neglected, so that the first would not be praised to the exclusion of the other, lest someone suppose that he was being blamed. Therefore He joined the praise of the other and commendation of him, along with preferring the first over him.

﴿And Allah is Acquainted with what you do﴾ That is: of spending in His cause, struggling against His enemies, and other than that, and He will recompense you for all of it.

Ibn Kathir said: By His knowledge, Most High, He distinguished between the reward of those who spent before the conquest and fought, and those who did so after it, and this is only because of His knowledge of the intention of the first, his complete sincerity, and his spending in a state of hardship, scarcity and constraint. In a hadith: "A dirham outweighed a hundred thousand," and there is no doubt among the people of faith that the Siddiq, Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, has the greatest share of this verse, for he is the leader of all who have acted upon it from among the nations of the prophets, for he spent all his wealth seeking the Face of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and no one had a favour upon him that he would repay with it.

And His Most High's words:

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, may He be exalted:

[11] ﴿Who is it that will lend to Allah a goodly loan, so that He may multiply it for him, and he will have a generous reward?﴾

﴿Who is it that will lend to Allah a goodly loan?﴾ Abu al-Su'ud said: It is an emphatic exhortation from Allah, exalted is He, to spend in His cause, after the command to do so, the rebuke for abandoning it, and the explanation of the ranks of those who spend. That is: who is it that spends his wealth in His cause, exalted is He, hoping that He will compensate him? For he is like one who lends to Him. The goodness of the spending lies in sincerity in it and in seeking the most noble wealth and the best avenues for it. Thus, "loan" is a metaphor for the good spending of one who gives sincerely in the best avenues of spending. This may be either by figurative use in the verb, in which case it is a continued explicit metaphor (isti'arah tabi'iyyah tasrihiyyah), or in the whole sentence, in which case it is a metaphorical image (isti'arah tamthiliyyah). Some have claimed that it is restricted to spending in fighting, and others to spending on dependants. Ibn Kathir said: The correct view is that it is more general than that; so whoever spends in the cause of Allah with a pure intention and a sincere resolve enters into the generality of this verse.

This is clear, and we have already explained it many times.

And His words, may He be exalted:

﴿So that He may multiply it for him﴾ That is, He gives him his reward in manifold multiples. ﴿And he will have a generous reward﴾ That is, a noble and beautiful recompense. The clause is either a circumstantial clause (hal), or a coordinated clause indicating that just as its quantity increases, its quality increases too.

(p-5681)

The discourse concerning the explanation of His, the Exalted's, words:

[12] ﴿On the Day you will see the believing men and the believing women, their light running before them and on their right hands. "Good news for you today: gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein. That is the great triumph."﴾

﴿On the Day you will see the believing men and the believing women, their light running before them and on their right hands﴾ means: because they are upon the straight path (al-sirat al-mustaqim), turning toward Him, the Exalted. The "light" (al-nur) is either literal and sensory, according to what has been related from Ibn Mas'ud: that their light is in proportion to their deeds, some of them having a light like a mountain, some having a light like a palm tree, some having a light like a standing man, and less than that. It has been said: these directions were specified because the records of deeds were taken from them, so God placed with them a light by which it is known that they are among the people of the right hand. Or it is figurative and metaphorical, meaning that which is a cause of salvation, and Ibn Jarir chose this and supported it with his statement: "If by that light He meant the known radiance, He would not have specified the report of its running as being before them and on their right hands, rather than on their left, since the radiance of the believers who are given it in the Hereafter illuminates everything around them. And in specifying the report of its running before them and on their right hands, rather than on their left, is an indication that what is meant by it is other than the radiance, even though they are not free of radiance." So the interpretation of the speech, given that the matter is as we have described, is: "And God has promised each the best reward, on the Day you see the believing men and the believing women, their reward for their faith and their righteous deeds running before them and on their right hands, and the books of their deeds flying." By "running" (yas'a) he means "proceeding." The particle "bi" (ba') in His words:

﴿and on their right hands﴾ carries the sense of "fi" (in). Some of the grammarians of Basra used to say: the "ba'" in His words ﴿and on their right hands﴾ carries the sense of "ʿala" (upon), and His words ﴿On the Day you see﴾ are connected (min silat) to "wa'ada" (He promised). End.

﴿"Good news for you today: gardens﴾ means: those who receive them from the angels will say to them: "Good news for you," that is, "the thing announced is gardens," or "your good news is entry into gardens." It has been said: the glad tidings may be given with the objects themselves, so there is no need to posit an omitted noun to make the attribution sound.

﴿beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein. That is the great triumph.﴾

**The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted Is He:**

[13] ﴿On the Day when the hypocrite men and the hypocrite women will say to those who believed, "Wait for us, that we may borrow some of your light." It will be said, "Turn back behind you and seek light." So a wall with a gate will be set up between them. Its inner side will have mercy, and its outer side will face the torment.﴾

﴿On the Day when the hypocrite men and the hypocrite women will say to those who believed, "Wait for us [unzurūnā], that we may borrow [naqtabis] some of your light"﴾ That is, "Let us take a flame from it." It is said *iqtabasa*, meaning he took a *qabas*, which is a burning brand. *Unzurūnā* means "look at us" (*unzurū ilaynā*), with the preposition omitted and the object connected directly, because *naẓar* in the sense of mere seeing takes *ilā* ("to"). If reflective consideration is intended, it takes *fī* ("in"). This statement of theirs is made either when the believers are driven to Paradise in groups while the hypocrites remain in the open place of judgment looking toward them, or when they look down from the chambers upon the hypocrites, who are in Hell amid their clamor and outcry. This is like His saying, Exalted is He:

﴿The companions of the Fire will call out to the companions of Paradise, "Pour upon us some water, or some of what Allah has provided you."﴾ [al-A'raf: 50], and the verse continues.

It has also been said that *unzurūnā* means "wait for us" (*intaẓirūnā*), and this is the view on which Ibn Jarir relied. The intended waiting for borrowing light then is the hope of their intercession on their behalf, or of entering Paradise with them, a hope that is pursued in what is not a hopeful matter. They say this when the believers are being hurried toward Paradise.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 57, verse 16:

The discussion of His saying, Exalted is He:

﴿Has the time not come﴾ i.e., has the time not arrived, from: anā al-amr ya'nā, when a matter came at its time (ināhu), i.e., its appointed time.

﴿for those who believe that their hearts should become humbly submissive to the remembrance of Allah﴾ i.e., that their hearts should soften, grow tender, and be sincerely devoted to the remembrance of His noble Name and to what it requires of awe (wajal) and fear (khashyah) of Him, or to the remembrance of His promise and His threat.

﴿and to what has been revealed of the truth﴾ meaning the Qur'an, which, had it been sent down upon a mountain, would have split it apart.

Abu al-Su'ud said: The meaning of khushu' to Him is complete submission to His commands and prohibitions, and devotion to acting upon what is in it of rulings, among which are what preceded and what followed concerning spending in the way of Allah, Exalted is He. It has been said that its conjunction with "the remembrance" is the conjunction of one of two attributes with the other, and that the remembrance of Allah is like the speech of Allah, meaning the Qur'an, and likewise "what has been revealed of the truth," so the conjunction is for the difference of the two designations, for it is both a remembrance and an admonition, just as it is a revealed truth.

﴿and that they should not be like those who were given the Scripture before, and the term seemed long to them﴾ i.e., the lifespan, the respite, and the extended delay (istidraj).

﴿so their hearts became hardened﴾ i.e., due to the departure of the fear and the awe that had come to them from the two Scriptures.

﴿And many of them are defiantly disobedient﴾ i.e., they went out from their religion, rejecting what was in their Scripture.

Note (tanbih):

Ibn Kathir said: The verse contains a prohibition for the believers against imitating those who were entrusted with the Scripture before them, from the Jews and the Christians. For when the term grew long for them, they altered the Book of Allah that was in their hands, bartered it for a small price, cast it behind their backs, turned to divergent opinions and crooked sayings, blindly followed men in the religion of Allah, and took their rabbis and monks as lords besides Allah. The statement on the interpretation of His words, Exalted is He:

[18–19] ﴿Indeed, the men who give charity and the women who give charity, and who lend to Allah a goodly loan – it will be multiplied for them, and for them is a noble reward.﴾ ﴿And those who believed in Allah and His messengers – those are the ṣiddīqūn (those of great truthfulness) and the martyrs with their Lord; for them is their reward and their light. ﴿Indeed, the men who give charity (al-muṣaddiqīn) and the women who give charity (al-muṣaddiqāt)﴾, meaning: those who give charity (al-mutaṣaddiqīn) and those who give charity (al-mutaṣaddiqāt) in the way of Allah. ﴿And who lend to Allah a goodly loan; it will be multiplied for them, and for them is a noble reward.﴾ ﴿And those who believed in Allah and His messengers – those are the ṣiddīqūn and the martyrs with their Lord; for them is their reward and their light.﴾ [al-Ḥadīd: 19] That is, because of their affirmation (taṣdīq) of all the reports and rulings of Allah, and their testimony to the truth of all of that. Two possibilities have been permitted regarding "al-shuhadā' (the martyrs)":

[p-5687] The first: that it is conjoined (ma'ṭūf) to what precedes it, so that He reports about those who believed that they are ṣiddīqūn and shuhadā'. This is the apparent meaning, because the basic principle is connection, not separation.

The second: that it is a new subject (mubtada'), whose predicate is "for them is their reward", and "al-shuhadā'" then means either the prophets, who bear witness against their peoples regarding the delivery of the message, or those who bear witness for the prophets against their peoples, or those who were killed in the way of Allah. Ibn Jarir (al-Ṭabarī) preferred the second possibility. He said: "Because faith, in common usage, does not necessarily entail that the believer is called a shahīd (martyr), in any sense other than that, unless it is meant as a witness to what he believed in and affirmed, in which case this would be a possibility, though it has some remoteness, because that is not the well-known meaning of the word when used without a connecting qualifier. So the interpretation of His words ﴿and the martyrs with their Lord﴾ [al-Ḥadīd: 19] would be: and the martyrs who were killed in the way of Allah, or who perished in His way, are with their Lord; they have the reward of Allah in the Hereafter and their light." End of quotation.

Then I saw, in Ibn al-Qayyim's "Ṭarīq al-Hijratayn" (The Path of the Two Migrations), an elaboration of these two possibilities in the discussion of ṣiddīqiyya (the rank of ṣiddīq). I transmit it for its excellence. He said, may Allah have mercy on him, regarding the ranks and categories of the accountable in the Hereafter:

The fourth category: the heirs of the messengers and their successors among their communities. They are those who uphold what they were sent with, in knowledge and in action, and who call people to Allah upon their path and method. This is the most excellent rank of creation after the messengers and prophethood, and it is the rank of ṣiddīqiyya. For this reason Allah linked them with the prophets in His Book, saying, Exalted is He:

﴿And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger – those will be with the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favour of the prophets, the ṣiddīqīn, the martyrs, and the righteous. And excellent are those as companions.﴾ [al-Nisā': 69] He placed the rank of ṣiddīqiyya as conjoined to the rank of prophethood. These are the rabbānīyūn (the godly scholars), who are "al-rāsikhūn fī al-'ilm" (those firmly grounded in knowledge), and they are the intermediaries between the Messenger and his community. They are his successors, his allies, his party, his intimates, and the bearers of his religion. It is guaranteed for them that they will not cease to be upon (p-5688) the truth; no one who forsakes them or opposes them will harm them, until the command of Allah comes while they are still upon that.

Glorified is He left out mention of the mixed-up person, the one with two mixed traits, following the Qur'anic manner in mentioning the happy and the wretched, and omitting the mixed-up ones in most cases, for a secret that His wisdom required. So let the one with mixed deeds beware, for he has no guarantee from Allah. He is not among the people of His unconditional promise, nor should he despair of Allah's mercy, for he is not among the disbelievers for whom punishment has been decreed. Rather, he stands between Paradise and Hell, between promise and threat, each of which calls him to its consequence, because he has come with its cause. This is what the proponents of the "intermediate position between two positions" (al-manzila bayn al-manzilatayn) took into account, but they erred regarding his eternal abiding in the Fire. Had they placed him between the two positions and left him to the will of Allah, they would have been correct. End of Ibn al-Qayyim's words, and in it there is agreement with what Ibn Jarir chose regarding the verse.

(p-5690) When He, Exalted is He, mentioned the happy ones and their final destination, He followed with mention of the wretched, and clarified their state with His words:

﴿And those who disbelieved and denied Our signs – those are the companions of Hellfire.﴾ [al-Ḥadīd: 19] Then He, Exalted is He, belittled the matter of this world and explained the outcome of its affair for its people, with His words:

﴿Know that the life of this world is but play and amusement, adornment and boasting among yourselves, and rivalry in wealth and children, like the rain whose vegetation pleases the disbelievers; then it dries up and you see it turning yellow; then it becomes debris. And in the Hereafter there is severe punishment, and forgiveness from Allah and His good pleasure. The life of this world is nothing but the enjoyment of delusion.﴾

﴿Know that the life of this world is but play﴾, i.e., a diversion for the soul. ﴿And amusement﴾, i.e., falsehood. ﴿And adornment﴾, i.e., a pleasing sight. ﴿And boasting among yourselves﴾, i.e., in lineage and ancestry. ﴿And rivalry in wealth and children, like the rain﴾, i.e., rain. ﴿Whose vegetation pleases the disbelievers﴾, i.e., the farmers. ﴿Then it dries up﴾, i.e., it withers after its greenness and freshness. ﴿Then you see it turning yellow﴾, i.e., from dryness. ﴿Then it becomes debris﴾, i.e., broken, crumbled stubble. Likewise, the world does not last, just as vegetation does not last. ﴿And in the Hereafter there is severe punishment﴾, i.e., for one who abandons obedience to Allah and withholds Allah's right. ﴿And forgiveness from Allah and good pleasure﴾, i.e., in the Hereafter, for one who obeys Allah and pays Allah's right from his wealth. ﴿The life of this world is nothing but the enjoyment of delusion.﴾

Al-Mahayimi said: Its possessor takes the playthings of this world in place of the playthings of the wide-eyed maidens of Paradise (al-ḥūr al-ʿīn), its amusement in place of the delights of Paradise, its adornment in place of the adornment of Paradise, boasting in place of boasting of being near to Allah in His presence, and rivalry in wealth and children in place of the blessings of Allah and the everlasting youths of Paradise.

When He belittled the sensory and psychic life, which is perishing, and depicted it in the image of green vegetation that quickly passes away, He called them to the lasting life. So Allah, exalted is He, said:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[21] ﴿Race to forgiveness from your Lord and a Garden as wide as the heaven and the earth, prepared for those who have believed in Allah and His messengers. That is the bounty of Allah; He gives it to whom He wills, and Allah is the possessor of great bounty.﴾

﴿Race to forgiveness from your Lord﴾ means: hasten to repentance from your sins, to attain forgiveness and pardon for your misdeeds from your Lord. ﴿And a Garden as wide as the heaven and the earth, prepared for those who have believed in Allah and His messengers﴾ means: the certain faith (al-iman al-yaqini).

﴿That﴾ means: the forgiveness and the Garden. ﴿is the bounty of Allah; He gives it to whom He wills﴾ means: to those who were worthy of it. ﴿And Allah is the possessor of great bounty.﴾ Ibn Jarir said: that is, by what He spread out for His creatures of provision in this world, bestowed upon them of blessings, and made them aware of the place of gratitude; then He rewarded them in the Hereafter for their obedience with what He described as having prepared for them.

In this there is a warning and an indication that the command to spend is for the benefit of the one who spends, not for any return to Him, exalted is He, for He is absolutely Free of need.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 57, verse 25:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

[25] ﴿We certainly sent Our messengers with clear proofs, and sent down with them the Book and the Balance so that people may uphold justice. And We sent down iron, wherein is great might and benefits for people, and so that Allah may know who supports Him and His messengers unseen. Indeed, Allah is Strong and Mighty.﴾

﴿We certainly sent Our messengers with clear proofs﴾ i.e., with decisive arguments and demonstrations confirming the truth of what they call to. ﴿And sent down with them the Book﴾ i.e., complete in judgment and rulings. ﴿And the Balance﴾ i.e., justice, as said by Mujahid, Qatadah and others. Ibn Kathir said: It is the truth to which sound and upright minds testify, opposing corrupt opinions. ﴿So that people may uphold justice﴾ i.e., with truth and fairness, which is following the messengers in what they were commanded and affirming them in what they reported. For what they brought is the truth beyond which there is no truth, as He said:

﴿And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled in truth and justice﴾ [al-An'am: 115], i.e., truthful in reports and just in commands and prohibitions. Hence the believers say when they settle in the chambers of the Gardens: ﴿All praise is due to Allah, who has guided us to this. And we would not have been guided if Allah had not guided us. Certainly the messengers of our Lord came with the truth﴾ [al-A'raf: 43].

﴿And We sent down iron, wherein is great might﴾ meaning fighting with it, for instruments of war are made from it. ﴿And benefits for people﴾ i.e., in their interests and livelihoods, for there is no craft except that iron has a hand in it.

If it is said: Conjoined clauses must have a connection (munasabah), and where is the connection between the sending down of iron and what precedes it?

The answer: There is a complete connection, because the intended purpose is to mention what completes the orderliness of the affairs of the world in this life so that they may attain happiness in the Hereafter. Whoever Allah guides from the elite intellectuals has his condition ordered in both abodes through the Books and the purified laws; and whoever from the common people obeys and follows them by implementing the just laws of the Shari'ah among them; and whoever rebels, transgresses and hardens is struck with iron that repels every rebellious one. He pointed to the first two with His saying:

(p-5694) ﴿And We sent down with them the Book and the Balance﴾, gathering them and their followers in one clause, and He pointed to the third with His saying:

﴿And We sent down the iron﴾. It is as if He said: We sent down that by which the elite are guided, and that by which those who do not follow them are guided. Thus the clauses are coordinated, not parenthetical for emphasis as is supposed, for there is no reason for that, and nothing in the speech requires it; rather, there is something that contradicts it. Al-Utbi said at the beginning of his "History": It occurred to me that there is incongruity in combining the Book, the Balance and the iron. I inquired about it but did not obtain what removes the difficulty and quenches the thirst, until I applied reflection, and I found that the Book is the statute of the Shari'ah and the constitution of the religious rulings, comprising the comprehensive rulings and limits, forbidding aggression and oppression, repelling transgression and enmity, and commanding equity and balance, and it could not be completed except by this instrument. Therefore He combined ﴿the Book and the Balance﴾. The common people are restrained to follow it only by the sword, the fierceness of its punishment, and the torment of its chastisement, which is the iron described by God as having fierce might. Thus with a brief saying He gathered meanings many in their branches, close in their extremities, firm in their beginnings and conclusions. Transmitted by al-Shihab.

Al-Qashani interpreted "the clear proofs" as knowledge and wisdom, "the Book" as writing, "the Balance" as justice, since it is its instrument, and "the iron" as the sword, since it is its material. He said: These are the matters by which the specific perfection is completed and the universal, which leads to the welfare of livelihood and the Hereafter, is regulated; for the principle of consideration and the first beginning is knowledge and wisdom. The principle relied upon for the perfection of the species, the uprightness on the path of perfection, is justice. Then the order is not regulated nor the welfare of the whole go on except by the sword and the pen, by which the affair of governance is completed. Thus the four are the pillars of the perfection of the species and the welfare of the multitude. It is also permissible that "the clear proofs" refer to theoretical knowledge and realities, "the Book" to the Shari'ah and practical wisdom, "the Balance" to acting with justice and equity, and "the iron" to coercion and repelling the evils of (p-5695) mankind. It has been said: "the clear proofs" are the true sciences, and the remaining three are the three well-known laws mentioned in the philosophical books: the Shari'ah, i.e., the law; the dinar that equalizes things in exchanges; and ownership. Whatever the case, they are matters that include the personal and species perfection in both abodes, since the perfection of the person is not attained except by knowledge and action, and the perfection of the species is not attained except by the sword and the pen. As for the first, it is evident; as for the second, man is civil by nature, in need of dealing and cooperation, and his livelihood cannot be realized except by association. Souls are either good, free by nature, submissive to the Shari'ah, or evil, slaves by nature, refusing the Shari'ah. The first are sufficed in their conduct by the path of perfection, the practice of justice, gentleness and the governance of the Shari'ah; the second necessarily need coercion and the governance of kingship. End.

Note:

Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah has a treatise on the meaning of the descent of the Qur'an and the word "descent" wherever it is mentioned in the Book of God Most High, in which he explained that many people interpreted descent in some places of the Qur'an in other than its well-known meaning, due to the apparent similarity of meaning in those places, and this became an argument for one who interprets the descent of the Qur'an by the interpretation of the people of innovation. He verified, may God have mercy on him, that there is no word "descent" in the Qur'an or the Sunnah except that it carries the well-known meaning of descent. He said: This is what befits the Qur'an, for it was revealed in the language of the Arabs, and the Arabs do not recognize "sent down" except in this sense; if another meaning were intended, it would be address in other than their language. Moreover, it is using a familiar word with a meaning in another meaning without explanation, and this is not permissible by what we have mentioned. He said: God, glory be to Him, mentioned the sending down of iron, while iron is created in mines. As for what is related from Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, that Adam, peace be upon him, descended from Paradise with five items of iron: the anvil, the tongs, the hammer, the pincers and the needle, that is a lie; the like of it is not established. Likewise the hadith narrated by al-Tha'labi from Ibn Umar, may God be pleased with them both, from the Prophet ﷺ, that God sent down four blessings from heaven to earth: iron, water, fire and salt, is a fabricated and false hadith, and people witness that this nation makes from the iron of mines what they desire.

(p-5696) If it is said: Adam, peace be upon him, descended with all the instruments, this is obstinacy against plain sight.

If it is said: Rather one instrument descended with him, and that is unknown; so what benefit is this to the rest of people? Then what would they do with these instruments if there were no existing iron to be beaten by them? And when God created iron, these instruments were made from it.

Then He informed that He sent down iron, so the greatest purpose in mentioning iron is making instruments of jihad from it, by which God and His Messenger ﷺ are supported. This did not descend from heaven.

If it is said: The instrument by which it is stamped descended. It is said: God informed that He sent down iron for these previously mentioned meanings, and the instrument alone is not sufficient; rather there must be a material from which the instruments of jihad are made.

He then said: Some have made the descent of iron mean creation, for He brought it out of the mines and taught them its craft, for iron only creates the mines, and mines are found only in the mountains; so God sends down iron from its mines which are in the mountains, so that the children of Adam may benefit from it. End of his words, may God have mercy on him.

And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And so that Allah may know who supports Him and His messengers unseen﴾, i.e., by using iron in striving against His enemies. It is coordinated with an omitted element indicated by what precedes it, i.e., that they may benefit from it and use it in jihad, and so that Allah may know... etc. He omitted the item coordinated with it, indicating that it is a prelude to what was mentioned, and this is its purpose. Or the lam is connected to an omitted element, i.e., He sent it down so that He may know... etc. The clause is coordinated with what precedes it, so the coordinated item was omitted and its complement was put in its place. It was also said: It is coordinated with ﴿so that people may uphold justice﴾. Al-Shihab said: This is close according to the wording, distant according to the meaning.

﴿Indeed, Allah is Strong﴾ i.e., over destroying whoever He wills to destroy, ﴿Mighty﴾ i.e., victorious and overpowering over whoever He wills.

(p-5697)

**The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:**

﴿And We certainly sent Noah and Abraham, and placed in their offspring prophethood and the Scripture. Among them is one who is guided, but many of them are defiantly disobedient.﴾ ﴿Then We sent, following in their footsteps, Our messengers. And We sent after them Jesus, son of Mary, and gave him the Gospel, and placed in the hearts of those who followed him compassion and mercy, and monasticism which they innovated. We did not prescribe it for them, except seeking the pleasure of God. But they did not observe it with its proper observance. So We gave those of them who believed their reward, but many of them are defiantly disobedient.﴾ [al-Hadid: 26–27]

﴿And We certainly sent Noah and Abraham, and placed in their offspring prophethood and the Scripture, so among them﴾, i.e., among the offspring, ﴿is one who is guided, but many of them are defiantly disobedient﴾, i.e., they have departed from His obedience by abandoning the texts of His Books and distorting them, preferring the opinions of the rabbis and monks over them, and committing what they were forbidden;

﴿Then We sent﴾ [al-Hadid: 27], i.e., We made to follow ﴿in their footsteps Our messengers. And We sent after them Jesus, son of Mary, and gave him the Gospel, and placed in the hearts of those who followed him compassion and mercy﴾ [al-Hadid: 27], i.e., tenderness and softness towards creation, because of the great emphasis Jesus, peace be upon him, placed on compassion, humility of the self, and love. At his time there were two nations of great harshness and severity: the Jews and the Romans. The latter were the harsher and more oppressive, especially in punishments. They had many varieties of torturing mankind, among them setting ferocious beasts upon them and training them for that purpose. The Christian mission came after them, struggled to pursue them, endured in confronting them, until it prevailed over them by His support and victory, exalted is He, as the end of Surat al-Saff has explained. ﴿And monasticism which they innovated. We did not prescribe it for them﴾ [al-Hadid: 27], i.e., We did not make it obligatory upon them; rather, they themselves committed to it of their own accord.

﴿Except seeking the pleasure of God﴾ [al-Hadid: 27]: this is a disjunctive exception (istithna' munqati', an exception not of the same category as what precedes), i.e., but they innovated it seeking to gain God's approval.

﴿But they did not observe it with its proper observance﴾ [al-Hadid: 27], i.e., they did not uphold what they had committed themselves to of it with its due upholding, in terms of asceticism, withdrawal for worship, and knowledge of the Scripture. Rather, they made it a tool for leadership, eminence, and subjugating the people to their desires.

﴿So We gave those of them who believed their reward﴾ [al-Hadid: 27], meaning those who believed with a faith pure of the taints of polytheism and innovation, and among them is belief in Muhammad, God's blessings be upon him, who was foretold among them.

﴿And many of them are defiantly disobedient﴾ [al-Hadid: 27], i.e., they have departed from the obligations of faith and its objectives.

**Remarks:**

**First:** Monasticism (rahbaniyya) is excessiveness in worship and austerity, withdrawal from people, preferring seclusion and celibacy. Its root is the verbal form attributed to the monks (ruhban), who are the fearful ones, on the pattern fa'lan, from rahiba, like khashyan from khashiya.

**Second:** Ibn Kathir said regarding His saying, exalted is He, ﴿But they did not observe it with its proper observance﴾ [al-Hadid: 27], that it is a censure of them in two respects:

One of them: in innovating in the religion of God what God did not command.

The second: in their failure to uphold what they had committed themselves to, which they claimed was a means of drawing near to God, mighty and majestic is He.

**Third:** I have seen in many works of later Christian scholars a condemnation of the innovation of monasticism and of the corruptions and harms its influence had on souls and morals. The author of "Rayhanat al-Nufus" among them said, in the seventeenth chapter, on monasticism:

"Monasticism arose from the delusion that withdrawal from associating with people, and the practice of ascetic disciplines and religious contemplations, are matters of great importance. But there is no support for this delusion in the Holy Books, because the example of Christ and the example of his apostles directly contradict it. For they did not withdraw from mixing with people in order to live in isolation; rather, they were always mixing with the world, teaching and advising. We say with complete boldness: there is no example of monasticism in the entire Holy Book, and there is no command of its commands that requires it. Rather, the opposite is true: the spirit and content of the Book oppose every claim founded on a solitary life coupled with asceticism. The Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on Surah 57, verse 28:

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[28] ﴿O you who believe, fear Allah and believe in His Messenger. He will give you a double portion of His mercy, and will appoint for you a light by which you will walk, and will forgive you. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

﴿O you who believe, fear Allah and believe in His Messenger. He will give you a double portion of His mercy, and will appoint for you a light by which you will walk, and will forgive you. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ Ibn Kathir said: Ibn 'Abbas understood this verse as referring to the believers among the People of the Book, and that they are given their reward twice, as in the verse in Surat al-Qasas. This is also found in the hadith of al-Sha'bi, from Abu Burda, from his father Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Three people will be given their reward twice: a man from the People of the Book who believed in his prophet and believed in me, for him are two rewards; a slave who fulfilled the right of Allah and the right of his master, for him are two rewards; and a man who educated his slave-girl well, then freed her and married her, for him are two rewards." Both al-Bukhari and Muslim recorded it in the two Sahih collections. Al-Dahhak, Utba ibn Abi Hakim and others agreed with Ibn 'Abbas in this interpretation, and it is the view preferred by Ibn Jarir.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: When the People of the Book boasted that they would be given their reward twice, Allah revealed this verse concerning this Ummah. The apparent meaning is that its wording is more general, and that its intended purpose is to urge everyone who has believed in the Prophet (ﷺ) to remain steadfast in faith, to be firmly rooted in it, and to submit to his commands. Among this is what He urged in the verses before it, regarding spending in His cause and generosity of soul in it, and that for them in return there is a abundant reward, as He said at the beginning of the surah:

﴿Those of you who believe and spend, for them is a great reward.﴾ [al-Hadid: 7]. So the end of the surah contains a return to its beginning, by reminding of what it commanded and of what its revelation was previously brought for.

The root of kifl (a share, a portion) is "the portion." Its root is what the rider places beneath himself to hold him steady and protect him from falling. The dual form in such a usage is either literal, or it is a metaphor for multiplication. And nur (light) is that by which one sees out of the blindness of ignorance and error, and which reveals the truth to the one who seeks it. As He, glorified is He, said:

﴿O you who believe, if you fear Allah, He will grant you a criterion, and will remove from you your misdeeds, and forgive you. And Allah is the possessor of great bounty.﴾ [al-Anfal: 29]

The discussion of His saying, Exalted is He:

[29] ﴿So that the People of the Scripture may know that they have no power over anything of the bounty of Allah, and that bounty is in the hand of Allah; He gives it to whomever He wills, and Allah is the Possessor of great bounty.﴾

﴿So that the People of the Scripture may know that they have no power over anything of the bounty of Allah, and that bounty is in the hand of Allah; He gives it to whomever He wills, and Allah is the Possessor of great bounty.﴾ is connected (mutaʿallaq) to the meaning of the imperative sentence (al-jumla al-ṭalabiyya), which implies the meaning of a condition. The implied sense is: "If you fear Allah and believe in His Messenger, He will give you what has been mentioned, so that the People of the Scripture who did not submit may know that they have no power over anything of the bounty of Allah, and that bounty is in the hand of Allah." By "bounty" is meant what He gave to the Muslims and singled them out with, because they used to see that Allah had preferred them over all of His creation. So Allah, majestic is His praise, informed them that He had given the community of Muhammad ﷺ bounty and honour that He had not given to them, so that they would know that they have no power over anything of the bounty of Allah, let alone that they could dispose of its greatest part, which is prophethood, so as to bestow it on whomever they wished. And that bounty is in the hand of Allah, not theirs, nor the hand of anyone else among the creatures; He gives it to whomever He wills of His servants.

The "lā" in "li-allā" is a redundant particle (ṣila). Al-Samin said: "It is a particle whose addition is widespread."

(p-5703) Ibn Jarir said: It is mentioned that in the reading of ʿAbd Allah (Ibn Masʿud) it is "li-kay yaʿlama" (so that he may know). He said: Because the Arabs make "lā" a redundant particle in every utterance in which a non-explicit negation occurs at its beginning or end, like His saying, in the preceding negation which was not made explicit: ﴿What prevented you from prostrating when I commanded you?﴾ [al-Aʿraf: 12], and His saying: ﴿And what will make you aware that when they come they will not believe?﴾ [al-Anʿam: 109], and His saying: ﴿And there is a prohibition upon a town which We have destroyed, that they will not return﴾ [al-Anbiya: 95], and the verse. The meaning of that is: "We have destroyed it, that they will return." End.

Al-Thaʿalibi, in Fiqh al-Lugha (The Jurisprudence of the Language), reported its addition in a number of examples in the section on the additions and redundant particles, which are among the customs of the Arabs. Consult it and you will increase in knowledge.
